source.command_latency_note: No separate command/actuation latency probe; setpoint issued and stepped at the same 0.05 s tick.

aggregation.detail: For each nominal speed tier take the maximum measured initial_speed_mps, the maximum measured along_m stopping distance and the maximum measured time_s independently (conservative envelope of the measured data, not a physics model).

measurement_basis.definition: Zero-velocity setpoint admitted and executed at the same 0.05 s tick; brake_distance_m is the measured displacement along the initial velocity direction from the actuation-start row to stable speed <= 0.08 m/s for 0.5 s; stop_time_s is that measured elapsed time. Measurement starts at actuation, so decision-to-actuation transport delay is NOT included and is added separately as robot_speed * action_delay (actuation basis). A trigger-to-stop measurement must use the trigger basis instead and must not add the reaction distance again.

notes: Measured in the current simulated vehicle/controller model only; not a real-flight or PX4 failsafe envelope.
36 episodes = 3 nominal speed tiers x 2 headings x 3 directions x 2 repeats, stopped from a valid zero-velocity v2 action.
No separate transport-latency probe: setpoint issued and stepped at the same 0.05 s tick.
Above supported_speed_range_mps[1] and below supported_speed_range_mps[0] no distance is extrapolated; the stop requirement is UNSUPPORTED at those speeds.
